Subject: Re: Renewal & expansion review - Acme Corp

Thanks James & Priya — great conversation earlier. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into procurement. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary pain: latency spikes on peak inference (recommendation calls) during promotional windows, and rising spend on embedding-based features (product recommendations).
- Current usage: ~2.1M inference tokens/day (avg), embeddings ~50k vectors/day, burst peaks ~4x baseline.
- Goals: reduce 95th percentile latency to <= 200ms for API recommendations, reduce per-vector embedding cost by ~25% or find caching strategy, and support new product-recommendation workload (vector search + reranking).

Proposed expansion path
- Short-term: Add a dedicated inference pool for recommendation workloads (pinned GPUs) to stabilize latency during peaks.
- Cost controls: Enable prefix caching for recommendations + batching for embeddings; estimate 15-30% token cost reduction.
- Timeline: Target procurement & PO by end of July; can start migration/baseline testing in August.

Open asks for Acme
- Confirm committed throughput target (requests/min or tokens/sec) for the recommendation service during peak windows.
- Confirm whether embeddings will be batched client-side or server-side (we can assist).
- Any procurement-specific requirements (SOW format, PO workflow, legal contacts).

Attachments: acme-usage-q2-2026.csv (usage export), proposed-pricing-acme-2026.pdf (draft pricing + options).

Next steps
1) You confirm committed throughput requirement and procurement timeline (PO cutoff).
2) We’ll produce a 12-month committed capacity quote + optional Dedicated pool configuration and a short SOW draft.
3) Meet next week for a 30-min pricing & architecture walkthrough if helpful.

Thanks again — I’ll loop Vivek on pricing once we have the throughput number.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0127

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and adding context: 

Confirmations / clarifications
- Pain points: correct — spike latency and embedding cost are our top issues. The recommendation service is customer-facing, so 95p latency matters.
- New workload: yes — we want to add a vector-search-driven product recommendations flow coupled with a light reranker. Expect ~200 QPS at peak initially (roughly 1.2k requests/min) and an average request size of ~1.2k tokens.
- Embeddings: we currently compute embeddings server-side in batches of ~128 but have room to change if that helps cost.

Procurement timeline
- We’re aiming to have an approved PO by 2026-07-30. Procurement will need an SOW and line-item pricing (monthly committed throughput + overage rates).
- Security: please include SOC 2 Type II evidence and our vendor security questionnaire — I can share it if you want.

Next steps
- Can you send a draft SOW and a committed-throughput pricing sheet by early next week? Also, can you share the SOC2 report link?
- Happy to do a 30-min follow-up on Mon/Tue next week — I’m flexible in the mornings PST.

Thanks — looking forward to the SOW.
